full_text_en:
Wang Guixue et al. v. Wang Yuande — inheritance dispute

Appellants (original defendants): Wang Guixue, male, 63 years old, worker at Harbin Workers' Sanatorium, Heilongjiang Province, currently residing at No. 135, South 14th Street, Daowai District, Harbin.

Appellants (original third parties): Wang Guigang, male, 47 years old, cadre at Harbin Taiping District Education Bureau, Heilongjiang Province, address same as above.

Appellant (original third party): Wang Shuxian, female, 50 years old, school doctor at Harbin No. 56 Middle School, Heilongjiang Province, currently residing at No. 2, Xuanhua Street, Nangang District, Harbin.

Appellee (original plaintiff): Wang Yuande, male, 31 years old, worker at Heilongjiang Provincial Academy of Social Sciences, currently residing at No. 74, Changchun Street, Daowai District, Harbin.

The three appellants, Wang Guixue, Wang Guigang, and Wang Shuxian, appealed against the civil judgment (1984) No. 621 rendered by the Daowai District People's Court of Harbin, Heilongjiang Province in the inheritance case, to the Harbin Intermediate People's Court.

The Harbin Intermediate People's Court found upon trial: The three appellants and the appellee Wang Yuande are in an uncle-nephew and aunt-nephew relationship. The decedents, Wang Mingyuan and Li Chunling, a married couple, died in 1963 and 1984 respectively. The decedents had five children born in wedlock: Wang Guixue, Wang Guifang, Wang Guichang, Wang Shuxian, and Wang Guigang. Wang Guichang died earlier, leaving no spouse or children. Wang Guifang died in 1954, leaving a spouse and three children born in wedlock: Wang Yuande, Wang Yuanwen, and Wang Yuanxia. In 1967, Wang Guifang's wife remarried, taking the three children with her. Although Wang Guifang's wife remarried taking the children with her, during the lifetime of the decedent Li Chunling, they frequently visited and cared for her, and on festivals they would visit and give food. When the decedent Li Chunling died, the appellee Wang Yuande contributed RMB 70 and joined Wang Guixue, Wang Guigang, and Wang Shuxian in handling the funeral. The decedents left a property of 83.507 square meters within the courtyard at No. 135, South 14th Street, Daowai District, which was occupied by Wang Guixue, Wang Guigang, and a non-party Zhou Hongfa respectively. After the death of the decedent Li Chunling, the appellee Wang Yuande filed a lawsuit with the Daowai District People's Court, claiming representation inheritance of the property left by the decedents. The court of first instance determined that the three appellants and the appellee had all fulfilled their support obligations to the decedents and were all lawful heirs. Therefore, it adjudged that the 83.507 square meters of property left by the decedents be inherited equally by the three appellants and the appellee, each inheriting 20.877 square meters. Based on the structure (number of rooms) of the property and the current living conditions of the parties, the actual division of the property was as follows: Wang Guixue inherits 21.487 square meters, Wang Guigang inherits 21.18 square meters, Wang Shuxian inherits 19.96 square meters, and Wang Yuande and his two siblings inherit 20.88 square meters by representation. The portions exceeding the equal inheritance share were offset by monetary payments: Wang Guixue, Wang Guigang, and Wang Yuande together paid RMB 82.50, which was received by Wang Shuxian. Dissatisfied with the above judgment, the three appellants appealed on the grounds that the appellee Wang Yuande's father had not fulfilled his support obligations to the decedents, and that Wang Yuande and his siblings, being younger-generation blood relatives, had no right to inherit the decedents' estate.

The Harbin Intermediate People's Court held upon trial: Although the appellee's father, Wang Guifang, predeceased the decedents, he had fulfilled his support obligations to the decedents during his lifetime and therefore should enjoy the right of inheritance. As for the appellee being a direct lineal descendant of a younger generation of Wang Guifang, in accordance with the relevant policies of China, he is entitled to inherit by representation the share of the estate that his father was entitled to. Therefore, the original judgment, which equally distributed the estate based on the parties' financial capacity to support the decedents at the time and in a manner conducive to living needs and without impairing use after the division of the estate, was appropriate. Accordingly, on May 7, 1985, in accordance with Article 151(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), the court rendered judgment dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

On November 29, 1985, the 237th meeting of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, in accordance with Article 11(1) of the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China, when summarizing trial experience, considered that in some places, especially in rural areas, there still exists the retrogressive custom of unjustifiably depriving children who go with their mother to a remarriage of their right to inherit their biological father's estate or to inherit by representation, which is inconsistent with the current legal provisions of China. Article 18 of the Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Husband and wife have the right to inherit each other's property. Parents and children have the right to inherit each other's property." Article 11 of the Inheritance Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where a child of the decedent predeceases the decedent, the direct lineal descendants of a younger generation of the deceased child shall inherit by representation. An heir by representation generally may only inherit the share of the estate that his father or mother was entitled to inherit." In trying inheritance cases in the future, people's courts at all levels should earnestly implement these provisions and effectively protect the lawful rights of children who go with their mother to a remarriage to inherit and to inherit by representation. The judgments of the Daowai District People's Court of Harbin and the Harbin Intermediate People's Court in this case are consistent with the above legal provisions and may serve as reference for people's courts at all levels.
